newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRIM TOPS TURNOVER WITH LARGE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRIM TOPS TURNOVER WITH LARGE TRADE.

text.p: Shares in Alan Jackson's rapidly-expanding industrial group Austrim Ltd topped the turnover lists on Friday when almost A$95 million worth of shares were traded.
Brokers said two lines of 9.5 million shares were traded at A$4.32 with ANZ Securities handling the trade.
At 1.20 p.m. (0320 GMT), Austrim shares were five cents lower at A$4.40 with 21.97 million shares traded.
ANZ Securities have done a lot of corporate work for Jackson, said one Sydney based broker.
"I don't believe it could be Jackson, especially since the company is in the middle of a rights issue," said the broker. "So it could be Kerry Stokes or (Richard) Pratt," he said.
Media entrepreneur Kerry Stokes and paper magnate Richard Pratt are major shareholders in Austrim, along with the Melbourne-based group's chief executive Alan Jackson.
On Monday, Pratt's Thornley Industries said in a shareholders notice that it had ceased to be a substantial shareholder in Austrim.
Austrim is currently raising A$208 million from a two-for-five rights issue.
Jackson, who ran the BTR industrial conglomerate in the United Kingdom for five years before returning to Australia at the start of 1996, plans to take up his rights entitlements.
Sources close to Austrim said Stokes also plans to take up his entitlements to the issue.
Austrim has a market capitalisation of A$694.12 million based on is 157.75 million shares on issue.
